indicators.note: ordering means putting into a new sequence, so the letters of the words before it are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, its S included
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Flora is busy arranging which plants to buy for the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flora' tempts as the definition, since flora means plants, but it is fodder: 'ordering' rearranges FLORASACTIVEIN into the answer, and 'plants' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: These are popular flowering houseplants of the saintpaulia genus, originally from East Africa.

explanation.surface: A card hand that a theatre boss would also long for.
explanation.walkthrough: In poker this hand is three of a kind plus a pair; in a theatre the same words mean every seat is sold, which is what a manager wants.
explanation.definitionFit: A poker holding of three matching cards and a pair, and also a sold-out auditorium.

indicators.note: coming here means emerging out of the words beside it, so the answer lies within them

explanation.surface: A Florida resident is coming back to their home state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming' signals letters that come out of 'Florida home': floRIDA HOme gives the run across the word join. 'State of Florida' pretends to be one phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A US state in the Pacific Northwest, capital Boise.

clue.text: Genius with tau cross is made a saint

indicators.note: cross here means mixed up or crossed over, telling us to rearrange the letters of the two words beside it

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A brilliant mind bearing a T-shaped tau cross is canonised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tau cross' reads as one thing, the T-shaped cross, but 'cross' is the anagram signal working on GENIUS plus TAU.
explanation.definitionFit: Augustine of Hippo, the early church father, is a canonised saint, as is Augustine of Canterbury.

indicators.note: to follow says the word for allowed comes after the abbreviation for Virginia

parts.note: VA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Virginia
to let is to allow, so allowed gives let

explanation.surface: A man was permitted to trail after someone called Virginia.
explanation.definitionFit: A gentleman's personal manservant, so 'man' in the sense of male servant.

indicators.note: arranging means putting in a new order, so the letters of song and sitar are reworked

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Musicians are arranging a song to be played with a sitar.
explanation.definitionFit: People who play a church or concert pipe instrument with keyboards are musicians.

clue.text: The best part of Japanese literature

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone praises the finest portion of the literature of Japan.
explanation.definitionFit: A select top group is the pick or cream of a larger body.

parts.note: she is the pronoun for a female
a is the indefinite article
the is the definite article

explanation.surface: Women's belongings are packed into a suitcase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'articles' does two jobs only in the sense of giving two grammatical articles: the indefinite and definite ones, set side by side after SHE.
explanation.definitionFit: To place a blade in its scabbard or cover is to enclose it.

explanation.surface: Oliver's life is full of unexpected turns.
explanation.walkthrough: Oliver Twist is the Dickens orphan, so 'Oliver's' gives his surname with 's; the same letters as a plural noun mean surprises in a plot.
explanation.definitionFit: Dickens's orphan bears the surname, and plot turns or surprises are also so called.

clue.text: Mrs Flintstone was in Luanda meeting Angolan leaders

indicators.note: leaders means the front letters of each of the words just before it

explanation.surface: A cartoon housewife turns up in the Angolan capital for talks with national leaders.
explanation.walkthrough: Luanda is the capital of Angola; the 'leaders' are not politicians but the first letters of 'was in Luanda meeting Angolan'.
explanation.definitionFit: Fred Flintstone's wife in the cartoon series The Flintstones has that first name.

clue.text: Brown coal by empty grate -it's explosive

indicators.note: empty means the word is emptied of its inside letters, keeping only its first and last

parts.note: lignite is the soft brown coal

explanation.surface: Brown coal heaped by an empty fireplace grate turns out to be explosive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'empty grate' keeps the first and last letters, G and E, which go before LIGNITE ('by' simply places them beside it).
explanation.definitionFit: A gelatinous blasting material made from nitroglycerine, used in quarrying, is a high explosive.

explanation.surface: Plenty of fish are found in railway carriages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trains' looks like a railway noun but is the verb: teaches or educates.
explanation.definitionFit: Large groups of fish swim together in shoals, and to educate someone is to teach them.

clue.text: Exceedingly small container — that is small-time

parts.note: a tin is a metal container
i.e. abbreviates id est, Latin for that is
S is short for small and T for time

explanation.surface: A very small container belongs to someone working only in a small-time way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'small-time' looks like one adjective but splits into S (small) and T (time).
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of minute or wee: smallest of all.

explanation.surface: Someone enjoying good vibes.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface recalls the phrase 'good vibrations', but 'Good' means healthy or reliable and 'vibrations' are what we hear.
explanation.definitionFit: Healthy or reliable, as in sound mind or sound advice; and noise, which consists of vibrations in the air.

clue.text: Famous climber, a fashion able youth in the 1950s, set off

indicators.note: in a down entry a climber goes up, so the word for famous is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: noted means famous
a Ted, short for Teddy boy, was a fashionable young man of 1950s Britain

explanation.surface: A celebrated mountaineer who was a stylish 1950s youngster set off on an expedition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Famous climber' suggests Hillary or Tenzing, but 'climber' turns NOTED upwards to DETON. Teddy boys were 1950s British youths in Edwardian-style suits.
explanation.definitionFit: To set off a bomb or charge is to make it explode.

parts.note: in means fashionable, as in the in thing
an essence is a scented extract used as perfume

explanation.surface: A fashionable perfume is described as being basic at heart.
explanation.definitionFit: At root or basically: describing the essential nature of something.

indicators.note: silly means foolish or muddled, so the letters of tax and decree are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone curses a foolish tax order.
explanation.definitionFit: To curse or denounce something bitterly, as a past-tense verb.

clue.text: Obsolete coin reintroduced in Pacific island?

parts.note: something reintroduced is brought out afresh, so it is new
the guinea was an old British gold coin worth 21 shillings, no longer minted

explanation.surface: A defunct coin is being brought back into circulation on an island in the Pacific.
explanation.walkthrough: The guinea is an old British coin worth 21 shillings; a reintroduced one would be a new one, so the two words build the island's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The large island north of Australia, shared by Indonesia and Papua New Guinea.

parts.note: overt means open or not hidden
here means present, as in answering a register

explanation.surface: Someone is told to open a gift over in that place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Open present' reads as an instruction to unwrap a gift, but both words are adjectives: open, and in attendance.
explanation.definitionFit: At that distant place, in the archaic or dialect sense of far off.

parts.note: Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet
ranges means spreads out or extends

explanation.surface: A man called Oscar is laying out some fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: Round citrus fruits with a bright peel, grown in warm climates.

clue.text: Agricultural worker presenting a pig to the queen

parts.note: a sow is a female pig
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the queen's royal cipher

explanation.surface: A farmhand presents a pig to the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who scatters seed in a field is a farm labourer.

clue.text: Animal seen by river is a skunk

parts.note: R is the map abbreviation for river
an otter is a river animal

explanation.surface: A creature spotted by the river turns out to be a skunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'skunk' points to the animal, but here it means a contemptible person. 'seen by' places R before OTTER.
explanation.definitionFit: A cad or contemptible fellow, in old-fashioned British slang.

clue.text: A strike leader given little money for rises

indicators.note: leader means the opening letter of the word strike

parts.note: cents are small units of money

explanation.surface: A union strike leader is given a small sum for pay rises.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rises' suggests pay increases, matching the strike, but it means climbs.
explanation.definitionFit: Climbs up a hill or mountain are upward journeys.

explanation.surface: An empty goal net.
explanation.walkthrough: 'net' is not the goal net but the adjective: after deductions, as in clear profit.
explanation.definitionFit: Free of contents, and after deductions, as in a sum earned in hand.

clue.text: Composer introducing symphony orchestra to America?

parts.note: SO is the usual abbreviation for symphony orchestra
USA is short for the United States of America

explanation.surface: A composer brings a symphony orchestra over to America.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the composer, though American, is a 'symphony orchestra' brought to 'America' only in the wordplay: 'introducing' places the first piece ahead of the second.
explanation.definitionFit: John Philip Sousa was the American bandmaster who wrote The Stars and Stripes Forever.

explanation.surface: Someone describes what happens after the polls close.
explanation.walkthrough: One sense is a second count of votes after a close election; 'say' is the verb, tell or narrate.
explanation.definitionFit: A second tally of ballots after a close poll, and to narrate a story.

explanation.surface: An animal is spotted in a river in Cornwall.
explanation.walkthrough: Cornwall is the county at England's south-west tip; its river of this name flows through Bodmin and Wadebridge.
explanation.definitionFit: A humped desert animal, and a river in Cornwall reaching the sea at Padstow.

clue.text: Rage wildly and gibe at a relative

indicators.note: wildly means in a disorderly way, so the letters of rage are thrown about

parts.note: taken as written
to taunt is to gibe at or jeer

explanation.surface: Someone loses their temper and mocks a family member.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rage wildly' reads as a verb phrase about losing one's temper, but 'wildly' is the anagram signal and the result goes in front of the word for 'gibe at'.
explanation.definitionFit: A parent's aunt is a family member two generations up.

indicators.note: part of says a run of letters is hidden within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A question about what a minister's property includes.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run from 'clergyMAN'S Estate'; the whole clue is also the definition, as the house is part of what a minister holds.
explanation.definitionFit: A Presbyterian or other minister's official residence belongs to the church living.

clue.text: A composer begot strife and glared dreadfully

parts.note: sired means fathered, begot
war is strife or conflict

indicators.note: dreadfully means badly, so the letters of glared are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A composer fathered conflict and stared about him in a fury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'begot strife' looks like a description of trouble-making, but each word is a synonym, and 'dreadfully' is the anagram signal on 'glared' alone.
explanation.definitionFit: The English composer of the Enigma Variations and Pomp and Circumstance marches.
